visible_text: What makes people complex: putting it all together
An individual's behavior is shaped by motives, preferences and competencies.
Motives as personal characteristics are quite stable over time
Preferences, by contrast, can partly evolve during the course of a lifetime
Competencies, thus, are directly related to learning.
As we saw, only behavior is easily and readily observable.
Human nature cannot be observed at all: it is a matter of conviction, or part of the social theories that we hold.
Problem is: observing behavior seduces us to (mis)judge others' competencies, motives, or even their nature.
An organization fit for complexity requires more reflection!
